text: The days that followed were a long strain, for whenever the steward came into my cabin to tidy it, my double had to slip into the bathroom or flatten himself behind my coats. <break time="0.8s" /> Once, as the steward opened the very bathroom where Leggatt stood hidden, my heart nearly stopped, but my double, crouching in the bath, somehow escaped his notice. <break time="0.8s" /> So intense was my double life that I began to speak in whispers even on deck, and my officers, seeing their captain start at nothing, must have thought him either ill or slightly mad. <break time="0.8s" /> Each order I gave seemed to come from a divided mind, half of it attending to the ship and half to the silent man in my cabin, whose fate depended entirely on my composure. <break time="0.8s" /> One night Leggatt told me, in his calm whisper, that he must leave the ship, because he would never let himself be taken ashore to face a judge and a jury. <break time="0.8s" /> He asked me instead to maroon him among the islands off the Cambodian shore, for he would rather wander the earth as an outcast than be shut up again in any cabin. <break time="0.8s" /> As I came at night, so I shall go, he said, and though I protested that he might never be found, I knew that he was right and that our secret could not last.
